pages.title: Money and accounts
pages.text: Six banknote denominations: 1, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100; face value equals exchange value.$(br2)A bank card has 9 slots for notes and records its owner and balance. Only at an ATM can notes be deposited or withdrawn by denomination.$(br2)Checkout debits the account; shop income can be withdrawn to a card. Insufficient balance cancels the deal.

pages.title: Price units
pages.text: Every buy price is quoted per $(bold)stack of 64$() — the same in $(thing)economic_product$(), in $(thing)products.entries$() and on the news page.$(br2)Daily movement: take the base price, roll an offset within base × $(thing)volatility_percent$()%, never below 0. The daily price is only shown on the news page; checkout still uses the shop entry's $(thing)price$().$(br2)Livestock and raw fish bought by weight do not use this system; see the next page.

pages.title: Buying by weight
pages.text: Two classes are priced per piece and never need 64:$(br)$(li)$(bold)Livestock in a woven sack$(): money = ceil( standard-weight price + max(0, actual weight − standard weight) × price per extra kg ). The weight is written into the item component $(thing)captured_weight$() (kg) at the moment of sacking: an animal with a stats panel uses $(thing)AnimalStats.weight$(), otherwise the species standard. Cats and dogs have no standard, so no component is written and the sack cannot be sold.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Weighable raw fish$(): money = ceil( jin × price per jin ). The jin comes from the $(thing)weighed_weight$() component; unweighed fish fall back to the mean of their weight distribution.$(br2)Both lists drift daily the same way: from the configured base price, a deterministic offset within ±20% keyed by day plus species/item (rounded to a cent), topped up with a little change when it lands on a whole yuan - so 10.00 never shows up. The Purchasing Box and the Prices tab share the same daily prices. On the Prices tab fish sit on the left and livestock on the right, both sorted high to low, and hovering a row highlights it.$(br2)Any item that can be weighed is removed from the $(thing)economic_product$() per-64 market so the two price systems never fight.

pages.title: Delivery orders
pages.text: $(li)Candidate pool: foods from the flavor_immersed_daily namespace prefix by default, expanded by takeout.extra_food_mods / takeout.allow_all_food_mods, then filtered by $(thing)food_blacklist$(), shuffled with the day's seed and cut to $(bold)40$() — the whole server sees the same menu on a given day.$(br)$(li)At most $(bold)3$() active orders; each times out after $(bold)8 minutes$().$(br)$(li)Pickup is 24~80 blocks from the player, drop-off 200~600 blocks.$(br)$(li)Pay = drop-off distance ÷ 10 (rounded), then clamped into the range formed by $(thing)takeout.min_delivery_fee$() and $(thing)takeout.max_delivery_fee$() (default 5~60 yuan).

pages.title: Shops
pages.text: Two kinds of shops:$(br)$(li)$(bold)System shops$() from $(thing)data/<namespace>/shop/*.json$(), plus the single "config shop" built from $(thing)shop.extra_entries$().$(br)$(li)$(bold)Player shops$() created at a Shopping Computer, limited by $(thing)player_shops_enabled$() and $(thing)max_shops_per_player$().$(br2)In an entry, $(thing)count$() is per purchase and $(thing)price$() is the total for that purchase.$(br2)When listing, players choose per item or per stack: a per-item entry has $(thing)count$() = 1 and the held stack goes in piece by piece; a per-stack entry has $(thing)count$() = the item's max stack size (usually 64), requires a full stack in hand, and buyers take a whole stack at once. Restocking converts using the entry's own unit, leaving any remainder in hand.$(br2)Every shop, system ones included, has a number in the Shopping Computer's left column and in $(thing)/fidashop list$(); the delete command uses that number, and creative mode can even remove the default system shops.$(br2)Besides the GUI, player shops can also be created and deleted with $(thing)/fidashop list|create|delete$(), but only for $(bold)your own$() shops; listing items, repricing and restocking still require the Shopping Computer.

pages.title: Third-party product discovery
pages.text: $(thing)auto_products$() is enabled by default; discovered products get a deterministic base price of 5~20 yuan per full item stack. Discovery uses common tags, crops and standard animal loot tables, excluding vanilla and the flavor_immersed_daily prefix. Explicit data-pack/manual prices take priority; add dynamic drops manually. See Economy Config for limits and blacklist syntax.
